title: Split local root subgroups and global Weyl representatives
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. An $A$-group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ satisfying the group diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $H$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $A$-group scheme whose geometric fibres are reductive: each is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] and has no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup. Unipotent means all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Let $S\hookrightarrow H$ be a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion], with a specified isomorphism $S\simeq\mathbf G_{m,A}^r$, $r\geq0$, whose geometric fibres are maximal tori; a torus over an algebraically closed field is a finite product of $\mathbf G_m$, and maximal means maximal for subgroup inclusion. Here $\mathbf G_{m,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[z,z^{-1}]$, with multiplication of units.
Write $M=\mathbf Z^r$; $m=(m_j)\in M$ defines the character $\chi_m(s)=\prod_j s_j^{m_j}$ of $S$. Let $\mathfrak h=\ker\bigl(H(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to H(A)\bigr)$, $\epsilon\mapsto0$, be the tangent $A$-module of $H$ at the identity, where $a\in A$ acts through the $A$-algebra map $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$ and addition is the group law. Conjugation by $S$ gives an $A$-linear coaction $\rho:\mathfrak h\to\mathfrak h\otimes_AA[M]$, $A[M]=A[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$ with $e^m=\prod_jz_j^{m_j}$, and $\mathfrak h_m=\{v\in\mathfrak h:\rho(v)=v\otimes e^m\}$ is its character-weight summand for the full torus coaction. There is a finite subset $\Phi\subset M\setminus\{0\}$, closed under negation, such that $\mathfrak h_m$ is free of rank one for $m\in\Phi$ and is zero for other nonzero $m$. For every algebraically closed field $F$ with $A\to F$, these characters are precisely the roots of $(H_F,S_F)$, with the usual character-weight meaning in [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. There is a homomorphism $\lambda:M\to\mathbf Z$ nonzero on $\Phi$; put $\Phi^+=\{\alpha\in\Phi:\lambda(\alpha)>0\}$, so $\Phi=\Phi^+\sqcup(-\Phi^+)$. For each $\alpha\in\Phi$ there is a closed $A$-subgroup $U_\alpha\subseteq H$ and an $S$-equivariant isomorphism $u_\alpha:\mathbf G_{a,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_\alpha$, where $\mathbf G_{a,A}=\operatorname{Spec}A[t]$ has addition and $s u_\alpha(t)s^{-1}=u_\alpha(\chi_\alpha(s)t)$. These subgroups become the corresponding root subgroups over every such $F$.
There are a finite group $W\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ preserving $\Phi$ and elements $n_w\in H(A)$, for $w\in W$, which normalize $S$, act on its characters by $\chi_{wm}(s)=\chi_m(n_w^{-1}s n_w)$, and satisfy $n_wU_\alpha n_w^{-1}=U_{w\alpha}$. For every $A\to F$ as above, $w\mapsto[n_w]$ identifies $W$ with $N_{H_F}(S_F)(F)/S_F(F)$, where the normalizer consists of elements preserving $S_F$ under conjugation. All character and root subgroup identifications commute with further algebraically closed field extension. If $\Phi=\varnothing$, take $W=\{1\}$ and the empty root subgroup family.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, introduction to Section 4, printed p.107 (weight subbundles); Definition 5.1.1 and its following discussion, p.136 (connected-base constancy); Theorem 4.1.4, p.110 (relative root groups); Proposition 5.1.6, p.138 (constant Weyl group); Corollary 5.1.11, pp.142-143 (global Weyl representatives). Local freeness of root lines becomes freeness over the local ring. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] to the conjugation action. Write $\mathfrak h=\bigoplus_m\mathfrak h_m$ with finite support and finite projective summands. At the unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] supplies $f\notin\mathfrak m$ such that $(\mathfrak h_m)_f$ is finite free. Such $f$ is a unit, so $\mathfrak h_m$ itself is finite free. Choose an algebraic closure $F_0$ of $A/\mathfrak m$. The tangent comparison identifies its rank with the dimension of the character-weight space on $H_{F_0}$. By [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections] every nonzero root weight there has dimension one and roots occur in opposite pairs. Let $\Phi$ be this finite nonzero weight set. Thus $\mathfrak h_m$ has rank one for $m\in\Phi$ and rank zero otherwise, and hence is zero in the latter case. The same base-change comparison for any algebraically closed $A$-field $F$ shows that its nonzero root weights are exactly $\Phi$.

source.place: Section 4 introduction, p.107; local freeness argument from Stacks Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective).

proof.text: For $r>0$, each $\alpha=(a_j)\in\Phi$ gives a nonzero integer polynomial $p_\alpha(T)=\sum_{j=1}^r a_jT^{j-1}$. Each has finitely many integer zeros, so choose an integer $N$ avoiding their finite union. Put $\lambda(m)=\sum_jm_jN^{j-1}$. Then $\lambda$ is additive and nonzero on $\Phi$. Since $\Phi=-\Phi$, its positive and negative values give the required disjoint union. For $\Phi=\varnothing$, including $r=0$, take $\lambda=0$.

source.place: Elementary choice of a regular integer functional on a finite set of nonzero lattice vectors; source Section 5.1, before Theorem 5.1.13.

proof.text: For each $\alpha\in\Phi$ choose a basis $X_\alpha$ of the free line $\mathfrak h_\alpha$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential], writing $U_\alpha$ for the closed image of $\exp_\alpha$. The map $t\mapsto tX_\alpha$ identifies $\mathbf G_{a,A}$ with its additive line group; composing with $\exp_\alpha$ gives $u_\alpha$. Its equivariance gives $s u_\alpha(t)s^{-1}=u_\alpha(\chi_\alpha(s)t)$ on all algebra-valued points. The cited theorem identifies every geometric fibre of this closed subgroup with the required root subgroup and supplies arbitrary base-change compatibility.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4, p.110; proof pp.116-118; trivialization of root lines over the local ring.

proof.text: We will use the following coefficient calculation for the local ring $A$. A group-like element $q=\sum_m a_me^m$ of a Laurent group algebra satisfies $a_m^2=a_m$, $a_ma_n=0$ for $m\ne n$, and $\sum_m a_m=1$, by comparing coefficients in $\Delta(q)=q\otimes q$ and the counit identity. A local ring has only idempotents $0,1$: either $a$ or $1-a$ is a unit and $a(1-a)=0$. Thus precisely one coefficient is $1$. It follows that every homomorphism between split tori over $A$ is a unique integer matrix of monomials, unchanged by scalar extension. In particular characters of $S$ are exactly $M$, cocharacters are $M^\vee$, and each normalizer element acts on $M$ by a single integral automorphism.

source.place: Section 4.1, p.107, characters of split tori; Definition 5.1.1 discussion, p.136. Coefficient verification written here.

proof.text: For $\alpha\in\Phi$, [lem-sfb-relative-opposite-root-reflection-map] gives a perfect pairing and a coroot. By the preceding coefficient calculation this coroot is a single $c_\alpha\in M^\vee$, with the same value on every geometric fibre. Choose $Y_\alpha\in\mathfrak h_{-\alpha}$ dual to $X_\alpha$, and put $v_\alpha=\exp_\alpha(X_\alpha)\exp_{-\alpha}(-Y_\alpha)\exp_\alpha(X_\alpha)\in H(A)$. It normalizes $S$. Its torus conjugation formula gives, with the character convention of the item, $m\mapsto s_\alpha(m)=m-c_\alpha(m)\alpha$; this reflection is its own inverse since $c_\alpha(\alpha)=2$. These are the usual root reflections on every geometric fibre, by the same cited statement.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.6 and Corollary 5.1.9(1), pp.120-121 and 140-141; explicit reflection construction in the proof of Corollary 5.1.11.

proof.text: Define $W\subseteq\operatorname{Aut}(M)$ to be the subgroup generated by these $s_\alpha$. For any algebraically closed $A$-field $F$, apply [lem-sfb-weyl-reflection-realization] to $(H_F,S_F)$. The split maximal torus $S_F$ lies in a Borel subgroup by [lem-sfb-torus-commuting-point-common-borel] with $c=1$; roots and coroots are those of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] for this pair. Restriction to the rational root span is injective on the normalizer quotient, and its image is generated by root reflections. Each such reflection is represented by $v_\alpha$ after base change, since by step 5 its coroot is the usual coroot on every geometric fibre, and its action on the full character lattice is $s_\alpha$. In particular an element acting trivially on $M$ acts trivially on the root span and is trivial in the quotient. Therefore every quotient element is a product of these representatives: choose a product with its restriction on the root span; injectivity makes that product equal to it in the quotient. It follows that the full character action identifies this quotient with $W$. In particular $W$ is finite and preserves $\Phi$, independently of $F$. For each $w$ choose a word $w=s_{\alpha_1}\cdots s_{\alpha_k}$ and set $n_w=v_{\alpha_1}\cdots v_{\alpha_k}$, with the empty word for $1$. Composition of the character actions proves the required formula, and the preceding identification proves $w\mapsto[n_w]$ is a group isomorphism on each fibre. No multiplicativity of the chosen lifts in $H(A)$ is required. If $\Phi=\varnothing$, the same injectivity on the zero root span makes every fibre quotient trivial; take $W=\{1\}$ and $n_1=1$.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.11 proof, pp.142-143, generation by reflections; classical Weyl reflection realization as stated in the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: It remains to verify subgroup conjugation over $A$. For $n=n_w$, differentiating its conjugation gives an isomorphism $d c_n:\mathfrak h_\alpha\to\mathfrak h_{w\alpha}$: explicitly $\operatorname{Ad}(s)d c_n(v)=d c_n(\operatorname{Ad}(n^{-1}sn)v)=\chi_\alpha(n^{-1}sn)d c_n(v)=\chi_{w\alpha}(s)d c_n(v)$. Its inverse is $d c_{n^{-1}}$. Consequently $c_n\circ\exp_\alpha\circ(d c_n)^{-1}$ is an $S$-equivariant map from the additive $w\alpha$-line to $H$ with tangent map the canonical inclusion. Uniqueness in [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential] identifies it with $\exp_{w\alpha}$. Taking closed images gives $n_wU_\alpha n_w^{-1}=U_{w\alpha}$. Finally each character is a fixed Laurent monomial, and every root map and each product defining $n_w$ base changes from $A$. The arbitrary and successive base-change clauses in [lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change] and [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential] therefore give exactly the asserted compatibility for further algebraically closed field extensions.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4, uniqueness and arbitrary base change, p.110; application to conjugation by a normalizer element.

proof_origin.place: Assembly follows Conrad Section 4 introduction, Theorem 4.1.4, Theorem 4.2.6 and Corollaries 5.1.9/5.1.11 read online. The literature copy is missing; WANTED recorded in report. Local coefficient and regular-functional arguments are written out.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q151-f6939ef29 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all three new nodes, every cited statement and the parent gauss-atlas in full. Conrad's Reductive group schemes is not in literature/; the worker filed WANTED and set proof_origin agent, so I checked the cited places against the standard statements (Thm 4.1.4 = SGA3 XXII 1.1, three-exponential element = SGA3 XX 3.1). Steps 1-5 and 7 are correct. Step 1: local freeness at the maximal ideal plus constant rank gives the same Φ on every geometric fibre. Step 4: the group-like idempotent argument holds over a local ring. Step 5: n^{-1}tn = t·α^∨(α(t))^{-1} is an involution and gives s_α(m) = m − c_α(m)α in the item's convention. Step 7: exponential uniqueness gives n_w U_α n_w^{-1} = U_{wα}. One fault, C4 in step 6: the Borel containing S_F was cited from lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure, which only asserts that some pair (T,B) exists. FIX: cite lem-sfb-torus-commuting-point-common-borel with c=1 (same unit; its closure adds nothing new and makes no cycle), and spell out the coroot agreement and the injectivity of W_F into Aut(M). The three new nodes are true, are not duplicates (relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer has no weight decomposition; the field nodes give no A-points and no relative uniqueness), and do not restate the item or the parent. Batch 5: the flagged paths end at lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent (Stacks 02VL), lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change (Stacks 021O) and lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection (split torus is smooth). These are generic sk-i-curve-zero facts, not trace-formula or Poincaré-duality steps, so they are acceptable. The prime-local-free tool use is accepted.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
